//: WHY py3.11 AND NOT py3.14: this repository runs two interpreters. LEAN is hosted by
pythonnet on 3.11; anything touching parquet runs on 3.14 because 3.11 has no pyarrow.
Checking against the LOWER version means the core stays importable by the LEAN side.
See quant_brain/core/provenance.py for the drift problem this belongs to.
WHY quant_brain AND tests ONLY: 673 of 1,042 function definitions across the repository
already carry return annotations and 87 of 97 files open with `from __future__ import
annotations` - the codebase is written as if it were type-checked and never has been.
That makes adoption cheap, but pointing a checker at 32k lines of five-day-old research
code produces a wall of findings nobody will action. Same two-tier reasoning as ruff.toml:
enforce on the shared core, leave the research surface to be brought in one module at a
time. `scripts/` is listed in `exclude`, not deleted, so widening the scope is a one-line
change when a module is ready.
WHY basic AND NOT strict: strict demands annotations on every parameter including test
fixtures, which buys very little on a codebase whose risk is wrong arithmetic rather than
wrong types. basic catches the class that actually bites here - Optional flowing into
code that assumes a value, and signature drift between the runners and shared modules,
which is precisely the 'trader/common drift gap' that commit ce7eb81 found by mutation
//reportMissingImports: warning, not error: tests import the runners as top-level modules (conftest.py puts
scripts/ on sys.path deliberately, so the import graph under test matches the one that
runs live). pyright cannot see that path manipulation, and making it an error would
report every runner import as broken when it is not.
